title: nem vs. nincs — Two Kinds of Negation

sections.content: nem negates identity or description (Ő nem a bátyám — He's not my older brother), while nincs negates existence or possession (Nincs húgom — I don't have a younger sister).
sections.title: Choosing the right negative

items.english: I don't have a younger sister.

items.spanish: Ő nem az öcsém, ő a bátyám.
items.english: He's not my younger brother, he's my older brother.

sections.content: nem sits before the word it negates and pairs with a form of 'to be' (Ő nem Anna); nincs replaces van entirely and means 'isn't there' or 'don't have' — don't write 'nem van' when nincs alone will do.
